title: Bet Hebrew Letter (ב): Sound & Dagesh
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Bet (ב): how the dagesh dot changes its sound between [b] and [v], with beginner explanations, example words and interactive practice.

editorialIssues.detail: Some mark-recognition distractors use letters not introduced in this lesson. Beginner scaffolding can be improved separately from the approved source synchronization.

blocks.text: Bet Hebrew Letter (ב): Dagesh, Sound & Practice

Bet (בּ) is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet. It is pronounced like the [b] in the English words "boat" and "boy." When pronounced, the lips come together to stop the airflow before releasing it.
In modern Hebrew, three letters — Bet, Kaf and Pe — can be pronounced in two different ways, depending on whether they contain a small dot called a "dagesh." One of them is Bet (בּ).
When Bet has a dagesh, it is pronounced [b] — a strong plosive sound like the "b" in "book."

blocks.text: The Hebrew word 'בָּא' [ba] means 'comes' in English. The first letter, Bet (בּ), has a dagesh and a kamatz gadol (ָ) underneath, resulting in the [ba] sound. Aleph (א) is silent in this case, so the correct pronunciation of 'בָּא' is [ba].
At the start of a word, Bet has a dagesh and is pronounced [b]. When a prefix such as ו (and) is attached, it can change to [v], as in וּבָנִים [u-vanim].
Without a dagesh, Bet is pronounced [v] — a soft sound like the "v" in "video."

The Hebrew word 'אֲבָל' [aval] means "but" in English. The first letter, Aleph (א), has a hataf patah (ֲ) underneath, producing the [a] sound. The Bet (ב) without a dagesh, combined with a kamatz gadol (ָ), results in [va]. The final letter, Lamed (ל), completes the word, making the correct pronunciation [a-va-l].

The Hebrew word 'אַבָּא' [aba] means "father." It consists of Aleph (א), Bet (בּ), and another Aleph (א). A patach (ַ) under the first Aleph gives the [a] sound, and a dagesh with a kamatz (ָ) under the Bet produce [ba]. The final Aleph is silent.

The Hebrew word 'בָּא' [ba] consists of Bet (בּ) and Aleph (א). The Bet has a dagesh, indicating a strong [b] sound. A kamatz (ָ) beneath it gives the [ba] sound. The Aleph does not have a vowel and remains silent.
This phrase consists of two words you have already learned: 'אַבָּא' (father) and 'בָּא' (comes). Try to pronounce them together smoothly.

You have now learned the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet and its two pronunciations. With these new letters, you can start forming words! Look at the examples, listen to their pronunciation, and pay attention to the vowels under the letters. Try to remember these words, as we will use them in future lessons.

exercises.prompt: Find the letter 'Bet' among the given Hebrew letters.
exercises.explanation: This is too easy a question, so go through it without hints. If you still need help, I have a cousin who knows a guy who can give you a hint… for a small fee!

exercises.prompt: The letter Bet (בּ) with a dot inside it (Dagesh) sounds like the [b] in the English word 'boat.'
exercises.explanation: When the Hebrew letter Bet (ב) has a Dagesh (dot) inside it, it represents the [b] sound, as in 'boat.'

exercises.prompt: When the Hebrew letter Bet (בָּ) is combined with Kamatz Gadol, what sound does it produce?
exercises.explanation: When Bet (בּ) is paired with Kamatz Gadol (ָ), it is pronounced [ba], like in 'father.'

exercises.prompt: The letter Bet (ב) without the dot (Dagesh) is pronounced like the [v] in 'vase.'
exercises.explanation: When Bet (ב) does not have a Dagesh, it represents the [v] sound.

exercises.prompt: What is the Hebrew word for 'father'?
exercises.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'father' is אַבָּא, pronounced [a-ba].

exercises.prompt: What is the Hebrew word for 'come'?
exercises.explanation: The Hebrew word for 'come' is בּוֹא, pronounced [bo].

exercises.prompt: When the letter Bet (ב) appears at the beginning of a word, does it usually have a dot (Dagesh) and sound like [b]?
exercises.explanation: In most cases, Bet at the beginning of a word has a Dagesh inside and is pronounced like [b]. However, exceptions exist in certain grammatical contexts — for example, when a prefix such as ו (and) is attached, as in וּבָנִים [u-vanim].

exercises.prompt: How do you pronounce the Hebrew word for 'father' (אַבָּא)?
exercises.explanation: The first letter, Aleph (אָ), with Kamatz Gadol represents the [a] sound. The second letter, Bet (בָּ), with Dagesh and Kamatz Gadol, sounds like [ba]. The final Aleph (א) is silent.

exercises.prompt: At the end of a word, Bet usually sounds like [b].
exercises.explanation: Word-final Bet is almost always pronounced [v], as in לֵב [lev].

exercises.prompt: What sound does Bet (בַּ) make when it has a Dagesh and is combined with Patah?
exercises.explanation: When Bet (בַּ) has a Dagesh inside and is combined with Patah, it makes the [ba] sound.

exercises.prompt: Which Hebrew vowel sign produces the [a] sound and consists of a horizontal line with two dots beside it?
exercises.explanation: The vowel sign with a horizontal line and two dots beside it is called 'Hataf Patah.' It represents a reduced [a] sound.

exercises.prompt: Which of the following Hebrew letters is marked with Kamatz Gadol?
exercises.explanation: Kamatz Gadol appears as a small 'T'-like symbol under the letter. When Bet (בָּ) is marked with Kamatz Gadol, it produces the [ba] sound.

exercises.prompt: Match each Hebrew letter or vowel combination with its correct phonetic value.
exercises.explanation: Dagesh in Bet produces a plosive [b] sound, while without it, Bet sounds like [v]. Patah and Kamatz Gadol both give the [a] sound, and Hataf Patah is a reduced [a].
